query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A neural network machine‐learning potential trained on an extensive set of ab initio configurations spanning both the disordered liquid and solid phases of multicomponent high‐entropy alloys near their melting temperatures will improve reference–target phase-space overlap and reduce thermodynamic integration path mismatch relative to standard EAM references.
generation.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high‐entropy alloys in solid and liquid states near their high melting temperatures.
generation.intervention: Develop and deploy a neural network machine‐learning potential trained on a diverse set of ab initio configurations that include both liquid and solid phase atomic environments.
generation.conditions: The intervention applies to high-entropy alloy compositions at or near their melting point, where the diversity in atomic configurations is highest and traditional EAM potentials have limitations.
generation.structural_mediator: The improved representation of local atomic environments—including disordered liquid structures and short-range ordering near melting—mediates a better overlap between the reference and target phase spaces.
generation.mechanism: By training on a comprehensive ab initio dataset that covers the full range of atomic configurations present in both phases, the machine-learning potential captures subtle interatomic interactions and structural fluctuations. This leads to a smoother, more continuous thermodynamic integration path compared to that obtained using standard EAM references.
generation.predicted_outcome: It is expected that using the machine-learning potential will noticeably reduce the thermodynamic integration path mismatch (on the order of roughly 20-30% improvement, though this magnitude is subject to uncertainty) relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references.
generation.baseline: Free-energy integration results obtained using TOR-TILD with standard EAM potentials for high-entropy alloys.
generation.boundary: This approach is specifically designed for multicomponent high-entropy alloys operating near their high melting temperatures. In elemental or simpler binary alloys where EAM potentials adequately capture the configuration space, the improvement may be negligible.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of the improvement (e.g., the 20-30% reduction) is uncertain and may vary across different alloy compositions and temperature conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct parallel thermodynamic integration calculations on representative high-entropy alloy systems near their melting temperatures using both the conventional EAM reference (via TOR-TILD) and the proposed neural network machine-learning potential. The MLP must be rigorously trained on ab initio data covering both liquid and solid configurations. Compare the free energy values derived and quantify the integration path mismatch for both methods.
measurements: Calculated free energies from the integration paths using both methods.
Quantitative assessment of phase-space overlap between reference and target configurations.
Metrics quantifying the length or discrepancy of the thermodynamic integration path.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the machine-learning potential does not result in at least a 15-20% reduction in the thermodynamic integration path mismatch, or similarly improved free energy consistency relative to the standard EAM reference in the tested conditions, the hypothesis will be falsified.

drafts.hypothesis: Replacing the standard EAM reference potentials used in TOR-TILD with a machine‐learned potential (MLP) that is trained on ab initio configurations spanning both the disordered liquid and solid phases will improve the overlap between the reference and target phase spaces and reduce the thermodynamic integration path mismatch.
drafts.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high‐entropy alloys in both solid and liquid states near their high melting temperatures.
drafts.intervention: Develop and deploy a neural network (or related machine‐learning) potential trained on an extensive set of ab initio configurations that include the diverse atomic environments of both liquid and solid high-entropy alloys.
drafts.conditions: The intervention should be applied to high-entropy alloy compositions at temperatures at or near the melting point, where atomic configuration diversity is maximum, and where traditional EAM references are known to underperform.
drafts.structural_mediator: The machine-learning potential’s ability to more accurately represent local atomic environments, including disordered liquid structures and short-range order present near melting, mediates improved phase-space overlap.
drafts.mechanism: By training on a broader and more representative set of ab initio data, the MLP can capture subtle interatomic interactions and structural fluctuations of high-entropy alloys. This reduces the mismatch between the reference and the target phase spaces during thermodynamic integration, leading to a shorter, more continuous integration path compared to that obtained with standard EAM references.
drafts.predicted_outcome: The application of a machine-learned potential is expected to reduce the thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by a noticeable margin (for instance, an estimated reduction on the order of 20–30% relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references), thereby improving free-energy calculations.
drafts.baseline: The free-energy integration results obtained using TOR-TILD with standard EAM references in high-entropy alloys.
drafts.boundary: This approach is specifically tailored for multicomponent high-entropy alloys near melting where atomic configuration diversity is high. In more conventional elemental or less complex binary alloys where EAM potentials capture the configuration space adequately, the improvement may be negligible.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform parallel thermodynamic integration calculations on a set of representative high-entropy alloy systems near their melting temperatures using both the conventional EAM reference (via TOR-TILD) and the proposed machine-learned potential. Ensure that the MLP is rigorously trained on ab initio data covering both liquid and solid phases. Compare the derived free energies and quantify the integration path mismatches.
measurements: Calculated free energies from the integration path using both methods.
Quantitative metrics of phase-space overlap between reference and target configurations.
Length or cost (e.g., computed work path discrepancy) of the thermodynamic integration path.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the machine-learned potential does not demonstrate at least a 15-20% reduction in the thermodynamic integration path mismatch (or comparable improvement in calculated free energies) relative to the standard EAM reference across the tested conditions, the hypothesis will be falsified.
